questions.stem: During the ingestion and digestion of a meal, peristaltic contractions are the primary type of contractions occurring in which of the following regions of the GI tract?
questions.solutionHtml:
Esophagus

Peristaltic contractions are the primary, if not the only, contractions of the esophagus that result in the rapid transfer of material from the mouth to the stomach.




Ganong's Review of Medical Physiology, 26th Edition, Page Number: 472.

questions.stem: Esophageal manometry is performed on a patient who is experiencing difficulty in swallowing. Between swallows, pressures above atmospheric pressure are recorded in the UES and LES, and pressures below atmospheric pressure are recorded in the thoracic esophageal body. Upon swallowing, the UES relaxes and a normal peristaltic contraction occurs in the upper esophagus. The peristaltic contraction occurring in the lower esophagus is slightly abnormal, but there is no relaxation of the LES. The defect in this patient most likely lies in which of the following structures?
questions.solutionHtml:
Intrinsic nerves of the esophagus

Normal resting pressures in the UES and LES, and normal peristalsis in the upper esophagus with swallowing indicate that the muscle, extrinsic nerves, and swallowing center are intact.




Ganong's Review of Medical Physiology, 26th Edition, Page Number: 473.

questions.stem: A disease that results in the loss of enteric inhibitory motor neurons to the musculature of the digestive tract will most likely be expressed as:

options.label: D
options.text: Achalasia of the lower esophageal sphincter

questions.answerText: Achalasia of the lower esophageal sphincter
questions.solutionHtml:
Achalasia of the lower esophageal sphincter

Achalasia is a primary esophageal disorder involving the body of the esophagus and lower esophageal sphincter affecting equally both genders and all ages.




Ganong's Review of Medical Physiology, 26th Edition, Page Number: 473.

questions.stem: A 39-year-old man presented with abdominal pain and diarrhea. On investigations, multiple ulcers were seen in the proximal and distal duodenum and in the jejunum. The gastric pH was found to be 1.2 with a serum gastrin concentration of 2000 pg/ml. Which of the following is the primary site for the production of GI hormone raised in this patient?
questions.solutionHtml:
Antrum

The given clinical scenario is suggestive of Zollinger-Ellison syndrome.

In this condition, serum gastrin concentration is raised to around >1000 pg/ml. Gastrin is primarily secreted by G cells present in the antrum of the stomach.




Ganong's Review of Medical Physiology, 26th Edition, Page Number: 456.

questions.stem: Examination of the properties of a normal sphincter in the digestive tract will show that:

options.label: A
options.text: Primary flow across the sphincter is unidirectional

options.label: B
options.text: The lower esophageal sphincter is relaxed at the onset of a migrating motor complex in the stomach

options.label: C
options.text: Blockade of the sphincter innervation by a local anesthetic causes the sphincter to relax

options.label: D
options.text: The manometric pressure in the lumen of the sphincter is less than the pressure detected in the lumen on either side of the sphincter

questions.answerText: Primary flow across the sphincter is unidirectional
questions.solutionHtml:
Primary flow across the sphincter is unidirectional

Primary flow across the sphincter is unidirectional the intrinsic and extrinsic sphincters operate together to permit the orderly flow of food into the stomach and to prevent the reflux of gastric contents into the esophagus the pyloric sphincter, prevents the reflux of duodenal contents into the stomach.




Ganong's Review of Medical Physiology, 26th Edition, Page Number: 445,472.

questions.stem: Slow waves are seen maximally in:
questions.solutionHtml:
Ileum

Slow waves are seen maximally in the ileum.




Guyton and Hall, Textbook of Medical Physiology, 14th Edition, Page Number: 838.

questions.stem: Iron absorption takes place in which part of the intestine?
questions.solutionHtml:
Duodenum

Iron absorption takes place in Duodenum.




Guyton and Hall, Textbook of Medical Physiology, 14th Edition, Page Number 830.

questions.stem: Surgical removal of a part of the stomach results in disturbed absorption of vitamin B12, which is excreted with feces. The patient was diagnosed with anemia. What factor is necessary for the absorption of this vitamin?
questions.solutionHtml:
Gastro Mucoprotein

The substance called intrinsic factor (Castle’s factor, gastro mucoprotein), essential for the absorption of vitamin B12 in the ileum, is secreted by the parietal cells of the stomach along with the secretion of hydrochloric acid.

 


Guyton and Hall, Textbook of Medical Physiology, 14th Edition, Page Number 888-890.
